vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: query() Async Iterator
vertices.description: The primary entry point for stateless, one-shot agent interactions. query() returns an AsyncIterator[Message] that yields messages as Claude works through a task. Covers the async for pattern, prompt types (string vs AsyncIterable), and when to use query() vs ClaudeSDKClient.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can write a complete query() call, iterate messages, handle ResultMessage, and explain when query() is appropriate vs ClaudeSDKClient
vertices.example: async for message in query(prompt='Fix failing tests', options=ClaudeAgentOptions(allowed_tools=['Read','Edit','Bash'], max_turns=30)): ...

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: ClaudeSDKClient Bidirectional Client
vertices.description: The stateful, bidirectional client for interactive conversations. Supports connect/disconnect lifecycle, async context manager, send follow-up queries based on responses, interrupt processing, set_permission_mode and set_model mid-conversation, receive_response convenience method, and MCP server management (get_mcp_status, reconnect, toggle).
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can build an interactive agent with ClaudeSDKClient using async context manager, send multiple queries, handle responses, and use interrupt/set_model mid-conversation
vertices.example: async with ClaudeSDKClient(options) as client: await client.query('Analyze this'); async for msg in client.receive_response(): ...

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: ClaudeAgentOptions Configuration
vertices.description: The central configuration dataclass that controls all aspects of agent behavior. Fields include: tools/allowed_tools/disallowed_tools for tool access, system_prompt, mcp_servers (dict of server configs), permission_mode, max_turns, max_budget_usd, model/fallback_model, hooks, can_use_tool, agents, sandbox, plugins, thinking, effort, output_format, include_partial_messages, resume/fork_session/continue_conversation, cwd/env/add_dirs, setting_sources, and betas.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the purpose and interaction of all major option groups, and configure options correctly for different use cases (autonomous agent, interactive UI, read-only analyzer, cost-limited batch)
vertices.example: ClaudeAgentOptions(allowed_tools=['Read','Bash'], mcp_servers={'db': db_server}, permission_mode='acceptEdits', max_budget_usd=1.0, setting_sources=['project'])

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Message Types & Lifecycle
vertices.description: The Message union type yielded by query()/receive_messages(): UserMessage (user input, tool results), AssistantMessage (agent response with content blocks), SystemMessage (session lifecycle — init, compact_boundary), ResultMessage (final result with cost/usage/session_id and subtype: success/error_max_turns/error_max_budget_usd/error_during_execution), StreamEvent (partial updates), RateLimitEvent. Also TaskStartedMessage, TaskProgressMessage, TaskNotificationMessage (SystemMessage subclasses for subagent lifecycle).
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can discriminate all message types using isinstance, extract content blocks from AssistantMessage, check ResultMessage.subtype for termination reason, and handle task notification messages for subagent monitoring
vertices.example: if isinstance(msg, ResultMessage): if msg.subtype == 'success': print(msg.result) elif msg.subtype == 'error_max_turns': print(f'Resume {msg.session_id}')

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Content Blocks
vertices.description: The four content block types within AssistantMessage.content: TextBlock(text) for text output, ThinkingBlock(thinking, signature) for extended thinking, ToolUseBlock(id, name, input) for tool call requests, ToolResultBlock(tool_use_id, content, is_error) for tool results. ContentBlock is the union type.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can identify and extract each block type from an AssistantMessage, access text from TextBlock, tool name/input from ToolUseBlock, and thinking content from ThinkingBlock
vertices.example: for block in msg.content: if isinstance(block, TextBlock): print(block.text) elif isinstance(block, ToolUseBlock): print(f'Tool: {block.name}')

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Custom Tool Creation
vertices.description: Creating in-process tools using the @tool(name, description, input_schema) decorator which returns SdkMcpTool. The handler is an async function receiving args dict, returning {'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '...'}]}. Input schemas can be simple dicts ({param: type}), or full JSON Schema. Error handling returns is_error: True. Tools run in-process — direct access to application state, no IPC overhead.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can create tools with @tool decorator using both simple and JSON Schema input schemas, implement proper error handling, and explain the in-process execution model
vertices.example: @tool('query_db', 'Query PostgreSQL', {'sql': str, 'params': list}) async def query_db(args): result = await db.fetch(args['sql']); return {'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': str(result)}]}

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: MCP Server Integration
vertices.description: Creating and configuring MCP servers: create_sdk_mcp_server(name, version, tools) for in-process SDK servers, plus McpStdioServerConfig (external subprocess), McpSSEServerConfig, McpHttpServerConfig. Tool naming convention: mcp__servername__toolname. Configuring via ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers dict. ClaudeSDKClient methods for runtime MCP management: get_mcp_status, reconnect_mcp_server, toggle_mcp_server.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can create SDK MCP servers, configure external MCP servers, use the mcp__server__tool naming convention in allowed_tools, and manage MCP server lifecycle at runtime
vertices.example: server = create_sdk_mcp_server('db-tools', tools=[query_db, insert_record]); options = ClaudeAgentOptions(mcp_servers={'db': server}, allowed_tools=['mcp__db-tools__query_db'])

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Hook System
vertices.description: Programmatic hooks that fire at specific points in the agent loop. HookMatcher(matcher, hooks, timeout) defines which tools/events to match. HookCallback is async (HookInput, tool_use_id, HookContext) -> HookJSONOutput. Hook events: PreToolUse (validate/block/modify tool calls), PostToolUse (audit outputs), PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact (archive before compaction), Notification, SubagentStart, PermissionRequest. Hooks run in your process, not the agent's context window.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can implement hooks for PreToolUse (block dangerous commands), PostToolUse (logging), and Stop (save state). Can explain hook execution model (in-process, not in context window) and the HookJSONOutput structure
vertices.example: async def audit_hook(input, tool_use_id, ctx): log(f'{input["tool_name"]}: {input["tool_input"]}'); return {'continue_': True}

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Permission System
vertices.description: Controlling what the agent can do. Permission modes: default (prompt for unknown tools), acceptEdits (auto-approve edits), plan (no execution, plan only), bypassPermissions (allow all — isolated environments only). Tool-level control: allowed_tools (auto-approve), disallowed_tools (block), scoped rules like Bash(npm:*). CanUseTool callback: async (tool_name, tool_input, ToolPermissionContext) -> PermissionResultAllow|Deny. PermissionUpdate for runtime rule changes.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can configure permission modes for different environments, implement CanUseTool callbacks, use scoped tool rules, and dynamically update permissions at runtime via PermissionUpdate
vertices.example: async def can_use(name, input, ctx): if name == 'Bash' and 'rm' in input.get('command',''): return PermissionResultDeny(message='Destructive command blocked'); return PermissionResultAllow()

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: AgentDefinition & Subagent Configuration
vertices.description: Defining custom subagents programmatically via ClaudeAgentOptions.agents dict. AgentDefinition(description, prompt, tools, model, skills, memory, mcpServers). Description drives automatic delegation — Claude matches tasks to subagents. Tools field restricts available tools (omit to inherit all). Model field overrides per-subagent (sonnet/opus/haiku/inherit). Subagents cannot spawn their own subagents. Agent tool must be in allowed_tools.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can design AgentDefinitions with appropriate descriptions (for automatic delegation), tool restrictions, and model overrides. Can explain context isolation — subagents get fresh context, only final message returns to parent
vertices.example: agents={'reviewer': AgentDefinition(description='Code review specialist', prompt='Review for security...', tools=['Read','Grep','Glob'], model='sonnet')}

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Subagent Lifecycle & Task Messages
vertices.description: Monitoring subagent execution through SystemMessage subclasses: TaskStartedMessage (task_id, description, session_id), TaskProgressMessage (task_id, usage with total_tokens/tool_uses/duration_ms), TaskNotificationMessage (task_id, status: completed/failed/stopped, output_file, summary). ClaudeSDKClient.stop_task(task_id) to stop running subagents. Subagents run in parallel for concurrent analysis. Resuming subagents via session_id and agent_id.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can detect subagent invocation via ToolUseBlock with name='Agent', monitor progress via task messages, stop runaway subagents, and resume subagents using captured session/agent IDs
vertices.example: if isinstance(msg, TaskNotificationMessage): if msg.status == 'completed': print(msg.summary) elif msg.status == 'failed': await client.stop_task(msg.task_id)

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Session Management
vertices.description: Persisting and resuming agent conversations. Sessions stored as local JSONL files in ~/.claude/projects/. Capture session_id from ResultMessage. Resume: options.resume=session_id (full context restored). Fork: options.fork_session=True with resume (new session branching from original). Continue: options.continue_conversation=True. Session data API: list_sessions(directory, limit, include_worktrees), get_session_messages(session_id, directory, limit, offset). Mutations: rename_session, tag_session. JSONL uses parentUuid chain — tree structure supporting branching.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can implement resume/fork patterns, use list_sessions and get_session_messages for session inspection, and explain the local JSONL storage model including the parentUuid chain structure
vertices.example: sessions = list_sessions(directory='/my/project'); msgs = get_session_messages(sessions[0].session_id); # Resume: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id, fork_session=True)

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Cost Control & Rate Limiting
vertices.description: Managing agent costs: max_budget_usd on ClaudeAgentOptions stops execution when budget hit (ResultMessage.subtype='error_max_budget_usd'). ResultMessage carries total_cost_usd, usage dict, num_turns, duration_ms. RateLimitEvent with RateLimitInfo (status: allowed/allowed_warning/rejected, resets_at, utilization, rate_limit_type). Model routing for cost: use cheaper models (Haiku) for routine tasks, expensive models for complex reasoning. max_turns as safety limit.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can configure budget limits, extract cost data from ResultMessage, handle rate limit events gracefully, and implement model-based cost optimization strategies
vertices.example: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(max_budget_usd=2.0, max_turns=50, model='claude-sonnet-4-6'); if isinstance(msg, ResultMessage): print(f'Cost: ${msg.total_cost_usd:.4f}')

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Context Window & Compaction
vertices.description: Understanding what consumes context: system prompt, CLAUDE.md (via setting_sources), tool definitions, conversation history, tool outputs. Automatic compaction when approaching limit — summarizes older history, emits SystemMessage with subtype='compact_boundary'. Prompt caching for static content (system prompt, tools). Strategies: use subagents for context isolation, selective tool loading via ToolSearch, lower effort for routine tasks. PreCompact hook for archiving. CLAUDE.md for persistent instructions (survives compaction).
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain context accumulation, compaction triggers, and strategies for keeping context efficient. Can use setting_sources for CLAUDE.md loading and explain why persistent instructions belong in CLAUDE.md rather than initial prompt
vertices.example: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(setting_sources=['project'], hooks={'PreCompact': [HookMatcher(hooks=[archive_transcript])]})

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Streaming & Real-time Output
vertices.description: Enabling real-time updates with include_partial_messages=True on ClaudeAgentOptions. StreamEvent messages contain raw API streaming events (text deltas, tool input chunks) with uuid, session_id, event dict, and optional parent_tool_use_id. Building real-time UIs that show text as it's generated and tool calls as they happen. ClaudeSDKClient.receive_response() as convenience for single-response workflows.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can enable streaming, handle StreamEvent messages to build a real-time UI, and explain the difference between StreamEvent (partial) and AssistantMessage (complete turn)
vertices.example: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(include_partial_messages=True); async for msg in query(prompt=p, options=options): if isinstance(msg, StreamEvent): process_delta(msg.event)

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Structured Output
vertices.description: Getting structured JSON responses via output_format on ClaudeAgentOptions. Format: {'type': 'json_schema', 'schema': {JSON Schema}}. ResultMessage.structured_output contains the parsed result. ResultMessage.subtype='error_max_structured_output_retries' when validation fails after retries.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can configure output_format with a JSON schema, extract structured_output from ResultMessage, and handle validation failure retries
vertices.example: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(output_format={'type': 'json_schema', 'schema': {'type': 'object', 'properties': {'summary': {'type': 'string'}}}})

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Thinking & Effort Configuration
vertices.description: Controlling reasoning depth. effort option: low (fast, minimal reasoning), medium (balanced), high (thorough), max (deepest analysis). ThinkingConfig: ThinkingConfigAdaptive (model decides), ThinkingConfigEnabled(budget_tokens) (visible chain-of-thought), ThinkingConfigDisabled. Effort and thinking are independent — effort controls depth per response, thinking produces visible reasoning blocks. ThinkingBlock in content shows the reasoning.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can explain the difference between effort and thinking, configure both for different use cases, and extract ThinkingBlock content from responses
vertices.example: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(effort='high', thinking={'type': 'enabled', 'budget_tokens': 10000})

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Model Selection & Routing
vertices.description: Choosing and switching models. ClaudeAgentOptions.model for initial selection, fallback_model for failover. Per-subagent model via AgentDefinition.model (sonnet/opus/haiku/inherit). ClaudeSDKClient.set_model(model) for mid-conversation switches. Cost-performance tradeoff: Haiku for simple tasks, Sonnet for standard work, Opus for complex reasoning. Dynamic factory pattern for subagent model selection based on runtime conditions.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can configure model routing with fallbacks, select appropriate models for subagents based on task complexity, and switch models mid-conversation using ClaudeSDKClient
vertices.example: def create_agent(level): return AgentDefinition(..., model='opus' if level == 'strict' else 'sonnet')

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Sandbox & Secure Deployment
vertices.description: Isolating agent execution with SandboxSettings: enabled flag, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, excludedCommands, allowUnsandboxedCommands. SandboxNetworkConfig for network isolation (allowUnixSockets, allowLocalBinding, proxy ports). SandboxIgnoreViolations for exceptions. Filesystem and network restrictions configured via permission rules (Read deny, Edit allow/deny, WebFetch allow/deny), not sandbox settings. Production deployment: Docker containers, credential proxies, never run bypassPermissions on shared systems.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can configure sandbox settings for different deployment environments, explain the separation between sandbox (bash isolation) and permission rules (filesystem/network), and design a secure production deployment
vertices.example: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(sandbox={'enabled': True, 'excludedCommands': ['docker'], 'network': {'allowLocalBinding': True}}, permission_mode='acceptEdits')

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Settings Sources & Plugin Integration
vertices.description: Loading project context: setting_sources=['user','project','local'] to load CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and agents from the filesystem. SdkPluginConfig for local plugins: {'type': 'local', 'path': '/path/to/plugin'}. Skills loaded only when settingSources configured AND Skill tool allowed. CLAUDE.md loaded into every request context (prompt cached). Project-level customization of agent behavior without changing code.
vertices.assessment_criteria: Can configure setting_sources to load project context, integrate plugins, and explain how CLAUDE.md and skills interact with the SDK agent
vertices.example: options = ClaudeAgentOptions(setting_sources=['project'], plugins=[{'type': 'local', 'path': '/path/to/my-plugin'}], allowed_tools=['Skill'])

frequency_analysis.analysis_notes: ClaudeAgentOptions is the universal gateway — every feature flows through it. Message types are the second gateway — you can't do anything useful without discriminating messages. Custom tools + MCP servers unlock the SDK's primary value proposition (extending Claude with your own capabilities). The top 5 components (options, query, messages, tools, MCP) cover ~70% of daily SDK usage. Hooks, permissions, and agents form the next tier for production systems. Session management, streaming, structured output, and sandbox are specialized concerns used less frequently but critical for specific use cases.

transfer_pathways.description: Configures hooks in settings.json daily. Conceptual understanding of PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop events is strong. Gap: programmatic HookCallback functions vs shell command hooks.
Uses permission modes (default, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions) daily. Understands allowed_tools from plugin/agent development. Gap: CanUseTool callback pattern and PermissionUpdate runtime changes.
Deep practical experience with compaction, prompt caching, and CLAUDE.md. Understands context costs from daily usage. Gap: programmatic PreCompact hooks and setting_sources configuration.

Creates and uses agents in .claude/agents/ directory daily. Understands agent descriptions, tools restrictions, model overrides. Gap: programmatic AgentDefinition in ClaudeAgentOptions vs filesystem-based agents.
Heavy plugin user and customizer. Understands the plugin/skill abstraction layer. Gap: SdkPluginConfig integration and setting_sources programmatic configuration.

Sees agent output daily but never programmatically discriminates message types. Conceptual understanding of tool use blocks, text, thinking from UI. Gap: isinstance checks, ResultMessage subtypes, TaskNotification messages.
Sees TextBlock, ToolUseBlock, ThinkingBlock in Claude Code output daily. Gap: programmatic extraction from AssistantMessage.content list.
Configures MCP servers in .mcp.json for plugins. Understands stdio/SSE server types. Gap: in-process SDK MCP servers via create_sdk_mcp_server, and the mcp__server__tool naming convention.
Expert Python including async/await. The async for pattern is familiar. Gap: this specific API surface — query() semantics, ClaudeAgentOptions, message iteration.
Expert with decorators, async functions, type hints. The @tool pattern will feel natural. Gap: the specific decorator signature, MCP response format, and the in-process execution model.

LangChain mental model: you build the agent loop yourself, manage message history, call the API directly. Agent SDK: the loop is managed by the CLI subprocess — you configure and observe, not build. Risk of trying to manage the loop manually when the SDK handles it.

LangChain tools are decorated Python functions called directly. SDK tools are MCP servers — the @tool decorator creates an MCP tool, not a direct function call. Different return format (MCP content blocks vs raw return).

Strong database skills provide the integration target. Building database query tools will leverage existing SQL/AGE/pgvector expertise. Gap: wrapping database operations in the @tool MCP handler pattern.

Systems architecture background provides understanding of isolation, credential management, network security. Gap: specific SandboxSettings configuration and the separation between sandbox (bash) and permission rules (filesystem/network).

failure_points.description: Trying to build the agent loop manually (LangChain mental model). The SDK manages the loop — you configure it via ClaudeAgentOptions and observe messages, not implement think-act-observe yourself.
failure_points.mitigation: Start with the simplest query() call and observe what messages come back. Let the SDK do the work. Explicitly contrast with LangChain: 'In LangChain you build the loop; in Agent SDK you configure it.'

failure_points.description: Forgetting the mcp__servername__toolname naming convention when adding custom tools to allowed_tools. Tools won't be auto-approved and will require permission prompts or be denied.
failure_points.mitigation: Always verify tool names match the mcp__server__tool format. Use get_mcp_status() to inspect available tools and their exact names.

failure_points.description: Using a string prompt with custom MCP tools in query(). Custom MCP tools require streaming input mode (async generator), not a simple string.
failure_points.mitigation: Use ClaudeSDKClient for custom tools (handles this automatically), or wrap prompt in an async generator when using query().

failure_points.description: Granting all tools to subagents. This wastes context (every tool definition adds to context) and increases risk of unintended actions. Subagents should have minimal tool sets.
failure_points.mitigation: Always specify the tools field on AgentDefinition. Read-only analysis agents get [Read, Grep, Glob]. Execution agents get Bash. Be deliberate.

failure_points.description: Understanding message types intellectually but struggling to build robust message handling code. The isinstance chain for UserMessage/AssistantMessage/SystemMessage/ResultMessage/StreamEvent/RateLimitEvent feels unwieldy.
failure_points.mitigation: Build a small message handler utility early. Most real code only needs ResultMessage (for final result + cost) and optionally AssistantMessage (for progress). Start there and add types as needed.

failure_points.description: Transition from single-agent to multi-agent thinking. Single agents are straightforward; multi-agent requires reasoning about context isolation, tool restrictions, model selection per agent, and communication patterns.
failure_points.mitigation: Start with the simplest multi-agent pattern: one orchestrator with two specialized subagents (e.g., reviewer + implementer). Build complexity incrementally.

failure_points.description: Assuming Claude Code CLI knowledge fully transfers to SDK programmatic control. Many concepts are similar (hooks, permissions, agents) but the programmatic interface has different patterns (callback functions vs shell commands, PermissionUpdate vs settings.json).
failure_points.mitigation: For each concept, explicitly map: 'In Claude Code CLI this is configured via X; in the SDK it's configured via Y.' Build the SDK version from scratch rather than assuming the CLI pattern translates directly.

failure_points.description: Difficulty designing effective hook chains for production systems. Individual hooks are simple; composing PreToolUse (validate) + PostToolUse (audit) + Stop (save state) + SubagentStart/Stop (monitoring) into a coherent system requires architectural thinking.
failure_points.mitigation: Design hooks as layers: security layer (PreToolUse blocking), observability layer (PostToolUse logging), state layer (Stop saving). Each layer is independent and composable.
